chapter: Armstrong, the Elite and New Orleans scene
title: Tom Anderson's place and old Rampart Street
summary: He describes Anderson's as the most exclusive spot, other nearby places, and the empty lots on Rampart.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Was Tom Anderson's a very, uh, jumping place? What happened there?

Well, that was about the most exclusive place they had around here at that time. Uh, Tom Anderson. Uh, Tom Anderson. Uh, it stayed back because, uh, we had another place there on, uh, Bienville between Ramport and Burgundy. Oh, I forgot, I forgot the name of the place. But anyway, that was where Manuel, uh, what's the name, Manuel Pures or somebody. Uh, I think, uh, who was playing trumpet around there. Uh, like, Big O was playing drums. And, uh, there's this girl, Sadie playing, uh, not Sadie. Uh, uh, Emma Barrett playing piano. Uh, who else was around there? Somebody else was around there playing. Uh, they kept a pretty nice crowd, but Tom Anderson was the leading place around here. At that time they only had, uh, Tom, uh, Tom Anderson in that block. The rest of that was all empty. There had a big Coca-Cola sign there on the corner of Ramport and Canal where that big, uh, five, ten cents to is. Nothing but a big Coca-Cola sign there at that time. All that was a big empty lot. Uh, the cars used to come up straight up, uh, Ramport Street to Canal Street and turn the trolley around and go back down to, uh, Industrial Canal or somewhere down there. And I was like, I went back down. Uh, on Sunday we used to have, uh, what they call an all-day picnic out at the lake. Used to have a train called Smokey Mary. I heard of it.
